comments.note: The MockErrorLogManager in error-log.test.ts faithfully replicates the real list() filtering/pagination logic. This is good for isolation but means any behavioral divergence in the real implementation could go undetected. Consider adding at least one integration-level smoke test using a real ErrorLogManager backed by a temp directory (as noted in the WP deliverables) in a future pass.

The test for 'defaults limit to 100 when not specified' asserts manager.lastListOptions?.limit === 100. This correctly validates the route's default, but lastListOptions will also have offset: undefined. Adding an explicit assertion that offset is undefined would lock down the full default parameter set and prevent silent regressions.

The mockRequest helper in error-log.test.ts does not accept a bodyJson parameter (unlike the one in repositories.test.ts). Since none of the error-log routes accept a request body this is fine for now, but if a POST/PATCH route is added later the helper will need to be extended.

comments.note: Removed dead `!Number.isFinite(id)` branch from GET /api/error-log/:id handler (src/server/routes/error-log.ts line 79). After the `/^\d+$/` regex guard, parseInt() can only produce a non-negative finite integer, so the isFinite check was always false. Updated the inline comment to accurately reflect the actual guard logic. Purely a clarity/dead-code fix — behavior is unchanged.

Query-string parsing (rawUrl.split('?')[1] + new URLSearchParams(...)) is inline in the GET /api/error-log handler — the only route in the codebase that does this. If additional routes need query-param parsing in future, consider extracting a parseQueryString(req) utility to requestUtils.ts to keep the pattern DRY. Not blocking at current scope.

[documentation-forward] The GET /api/error-log route has no module-level JSDoc or API surface documentation beyond the route registration table comment. A future documentation pass should add: (1) description of all supported query parameters (severity, source, limit, offset) with their types, defaults, and validation rules; (2) note that limit defaults to 100 to prevent unbounded queries; (3) description of the { entries, total } response shape. This would make the API discoverable without reading the implementation.

The `manager as never` cast in error-log.test.ts line 107 correctly bypasses the type incompatibility between MockErrorLogManager and ErrorLogManager (which requires AppConfig in its constructor). A slightly less aggressive cast (`manager as unknown as ErrorLogManager`) would be more conventional, but both are equivalent at runtime. Low priority — acceptable test idiom.
